ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
Faster, Higher, Stronger: What Innovations Bring

Five sprinters were getting ready at the starting line of the men's 100-meter sprint in 1896 when the first modern Olympic Games were held. One sprinter in particular caught the spectators' attention. He was touching the ground with his hips raised towards the sky, while the others were simply standing. The spectators laughed at the position of his body, but it took only 11.8 seconds for them to witness him setting the first Olympic record. This sprinter's name was Thomas Burke, and his innovative technique called a crouch start has become the standard starting position since then. Here are some key innovations introduced by great athletes who challenged themselves to find what worked best. They proved that there is always room for improvement.

The Flip Turn in Swimming

Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an open turn. They touched the wall with one or two hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns had the critical disadvantage of disrupting the swimmers' flow and speed.

This problem was resolved by an American high school student named Al Vande Weghe. While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. To overcome this drawback, he devised a technique that is now known as a flip turn. He would make a forward roll first to change direction and then kick against the wall to speed ahead. This technique allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible. His willingness to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in freestyle and backstroke races.

The V Style in Ski Jumping

Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of 90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the air for about five to seven seconds. While they are in the air, they are influenced by "lift," an upward force produced by air on a fast-moving object. When the force of lift is balanced with the force of gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The key factors for them to increase lift and jumping distance are increasing their speed, spreading out their bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle.

As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance as well as their style, skiers have tried many techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump. Later, this upright style was replaced by the Kongsberger style. The skiers' upper body was bent at the hips, with their arms extended in front of them and their skis parallel to each other. This technique doubled the average jumping distance.

Everything changed in 1985, however, when Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style. In this style, the skiers position their skis into a "V" shape with their heads placed between the skis. This modification increases the surface area and creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping distances. Wind tunnel tests showed that the V style improves air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury.

The V style was not immediately adopted by the skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed and received few style points for breaking the standard of parallel skis. However, the technique proved so successful that by 1992 all Olympic medalists were using it.

The Fosbury Flop in High Jumping

Dick Fosbury practiced the major high jump techniques, such as the scissors and the straddle, for the Olympics when he was in high school. He soon realized, however, that these techniques were challenging for him because he didn't have the strength or speed they require. Then he found that when he went over the bar backward and landed headfirst, he could jump higher than anyone on his team. As an engineering major, he later explained that arching the body backward keeps the jumper's center of gravity low to the ground. The lower the center of gravity, the less energy required to successfully jump over the bar. Another advantage is that with this technique, there is less chance that the jumper's arms or legs will hit the bar and knock it down.

The result was a huge success. Fosbury won a gold medal in the high jump in the 1968 Olympics. But up to that point, every jumper in the event had only gone over the bar forward, not backward. Local newspapers criticized his style, saying that he looked like "a fish flopping in a boat" and calling him "the world's laziest high jumper." Eight years later, however, 90% of all high jumpers were going over the bar backward just like Fosbury. Today, every high jumper performs what is known as the "Fosbury Flop."

Athletes often face challenges when they realize that conventional techniques aren't working out for them. They then make determined efforts to overcome these weaknesses. Some of these athletes end up developing remarkable innovative techniques, which eventually become the new norm. Innovation flourishes when individuals have a deep understanding of themselves and discover their own unique strengths.

questions.passage: The spectators laughed at the position of his body, but it took only 11. 8 seconds for them to witness him setting the first Olympic record. This sprinter's name was Thomas Burke, and his (A)[innovative / traditional] technique called a crouch start has become the (B)[standard / temporary] starting position since then. Here are some key innovations introduced by great athletes who challenged themselves to find what worked best. They proved that there is always room for (C)[improvement / room].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그의 혁신적인(innovative) 기법은 표준적인(standard) 출발 자세가 되었고, 항상 개선(improvement)의 여지가 있음을 증명했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② innovative — standard — improvement: 원문 일치
❌ ① room: 'room for improvement'가 관용구이므로 improvement가 맞음
❌ ③ traditional(전통적인): 새로운 기법이므로 innovative가 맞음
❌ ④ temporary(임시적인): 지금까지 이어지는 표준이므로 standard가 맞음
det.tip: innovative(혁신적인) ↔ traditional(전통적인). standard(표준적인) ↔ temporary(임시적인). 'room for improvement' = 개선의 여지.

They touched the wall with one or two hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns had the critical (A)[disadvantage / advantage] of disrupting the swimmers' flow and speed. This problem was resolved by an American high school student named Al Vande Weghe. While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. To overcome this drawback, he (B)[devised / abandoned] a technique that is now known as a flip turn. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 오픈 턴은 속도를 방해하는 단점(disadvantage)이 있었고, 그는 새 기법을 고안했으며(devised), 이 기법으로 추진력(momentum)을 유지할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① disadvantage — devised — momentum: 원문 일치

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 변형(modification)은 표면적을 증가시켜(increases) 더 큰 점프 거리를 이끌었지만, 처음에는 조롱받았다(ridiculed).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ modification — increases — ridiculed: 원문 일치
❌ ① reduces(줄인다): 표면적이 증가해야 양력이 커짐
❌ ② celebrated(환영받은): 처음에는 조롱받았다는 내용

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① spectators(관중): 원문 일치

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'increasing(증가시키는)'인데, 'decreasing(감소시키는)'으로 바뀌었다. 양력과 점프 거리를 증가시키려면 속도를 높여야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① spectacular(장관인): 원문 일치
✅ ② balanced(균형 잡힌): 원문 일치
❌ ③ decreasing(감소시키는) → increasing(증가시키는): 속도를 줄이면 양력이 줄어 점프 거리가 짧아짐
✅ ④ adjusting(조정하는): 원문 일치
det.tip: increasing(증가시키다) ↔ decreasing(감소시키다). 'increase lift and jumping distance'가 목적.

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'less(더 적은)'인데, 'more(더 많은)'로 바뀌었다. 무게중심이 낮을수록 필요 에너지가 '적다'는 것이 장점이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① challenging(어려운): 원문 일치
✅ ② backward(뒤로): 원문 일치
✅ ③ center(중심): 원문 일치
❌ ④ more(더 많은) → less(더 적은): 무게중심이 낮을수록 에너지가 적게 필요하다는 장점
det.tip: less(더 적은) ↔ more(더 많은). 'Another advantage'가 단서: 장점 = 바를 칠 확률이 줄어든다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 오픈 턴의 단점(drawback)을 극복하기 위해 플립 턴을 고안했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ drawback(단점): 원문 일치. 'overcome this ____'에서 극복 대상 = 단점
❌ ① position(위치): 극복할 대상이 아님
❌ ② technique(기법): 기법을 극복한다는 표현 부적절
❌ ③ advantage(장점): 장점을 극복한다는 의미 모순
det.tip: drawback = disadvantage = 단점. 'overcome(극복하다)'과 어울리는 부정적 의미의 단어.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: V 스타일은 표면(surface)적을 증가시켜 더 큰 양력을 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② surface(표면): 원문 일치. 'surface area(표면적)'가 증가하면 양력이 커짐
❌ ① distance(거리): '거리 면적'은 어색
❌ ③ jumping(점프): 'jumping area'는 표면적 개념이 아님
❌ ④ parallel(평행한): 평행 스키가 아닌 V자로 바꾸는 것
det.tip: surface area = 표면적. V자로 스키를 벌리면 공기와 닿는 면적이 넓어져 양력 증가.

det.korean: 스키 선수들은 공중에 머무는 시간을 극대화하려(maximize) 다양한 기법을 시도했다.
det.analysis:

questions.passage: The V style was not immediately <u>adopted</u> by the skiing community.  In fact, it was initially ridiculed and received few style points for breaking the standard of parallel skis.

✅ ① rejected(거부하다): adopted의 반의어

(B) She <u>set</u> the vase carefully on the table.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 setting과 가장 가까운 의미로 쓰인 것은?

det.korean: 'setting the first Olympic record'에서 set은 '수립하다/세우다'의 의미. (A)는 '마감일을 정하다'로 유사하고, (B)는 '놓다'의 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A): set a deadline = 마감일을 정하다. set a record = 기록을 수립하다. 둘 다 '정하다/세우다' 의미
❌ ② (B): set the vase = 꽃병을 놓다. 물리적 배치 의미
❌ ③ 모두: (B)는 다른 의미
❌ ④ 둘 다 아님: (A)가 가까운 의미
det.tip: set: 기록/기준/마감일을 세우다 vs 물건을 놓다. 'set a record'는 '기록을 수립하다'.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a strong desire or readiness to do something, especially something that involves risk or difficulty"

det.korean: '위험이나 어려움이 수반되는 일을 하려는 강한 의지나 준비 상태' = willingness(의지/자발성).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ willingness(의지): 본문 'His willingness to take a risk'와 일치하는 영영 정의
❌ ① momentum(추진력): 물리적 운동량
❌ ② technique(기법): 방법/기술
❌ ④ advantage(장점): 유리한 점
det.tip: willingness = 기꺼이 ~하려는 마음. willing(기꺼이 하는) + -ness(명사 접미사).

questions.passage: He soon realized, however, that these techniques were __________ (challenge) for him because he didn't have the strength or speed they require.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 이 기법들은 그에게 도전적인/어려운(challenging) 것이었다.
det.analysis: challenge → challenging: be동사(were) 뒤에 보어로 형용사 필요. '~에게 어려운'이라는 의미의 현재분사형 형용사.
det.tip: challenge(n. 도전) → challenging(adj. 어려운/도전적인). 'be challenging for ~' = ~에게 어렵다.

questions.passage: The lower the center of gravity, the less energy required to __________ (successful) jump over the bar.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 바를 성공적으로(successfully) 넘기 위해 필요한 에너지가 적어진다.
det.analysis: successful → successfully: 동사 'jump'를 수식해야 하므로 부사형 필요. to부정사 구문에서 동사 앞 부사 위치.
det.tip: successful(adj. 성공적인) → successfully(adv. 성공적으로). 동사 수식 = 부사.

questions.passage: To overcome this drawback, he devised a technique that is now known as a flip turn.  He would make a forward roll first to change direction and then kick against the wall to speed ahead.  This technique allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible.  His willingness to take a risk and keep experimenting __________.  Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 위험을 감수하고 계속 실험하려는 그의 의지는 성과를 거뒀다(paid off).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ paid off(성과를 거뒀다): 원문 일치. 은메달 수상이라는 성과로 이어졌음
❌ ① taking a risk(위험을 감수하다): 이미 앞에 나온 표현
❌ ② changing direction(방향을 바꾸다): 플립 턴의 동작이지 의지의 결과가 아님
❌ ④ slowed down(느려졌다): 문맥상 반대. 실험이 성공해서 메달을 땄음
det.tip: paid off = 성과를 거두다/보람이 있다. 'His willingness ... paid off'에서 노력 → 결과 구조.

questions.passage:
"

Athletes often face challenges when they realize that conventional techniques aren't working out for them.  They then make determined efforts to overcome these weaknesses.  Some of these athletes end up developing remarkable innovative techniques, which eventually become the new norm.  Innovation flourishes when individuals have __________ and discover their own unique strengths.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혁신은 개인이 자기 자신에 대한 깊은 이해(a deep understanding of themselves)를 갖고 자신만의 독특한 강점을 발견할 때 꽃핀다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② a deep understanding of themselves: 원문 일치. 혁신의 조건
❌ ① the new norm(새로운 표준): 혁신의 결과이지 조건이 아님
❌ ③ remarkable innovative techniques(놀라운 혁신 기법): 혁신의 산물이지 선행 조건이 아님
❌ ④ determined efforts(결연한 노력): 중간 과정이지 'flourishes when ~' 뒤의 조건이 아님
det.tip: Innovation flourishes when ~ = 혁신이 꽃피는 조건. 자기 이해 → 강점 발견 → 혁신.
